what: Dutch Bros runs drive-through coffee shops, mostly in the western and southern United States. It sells coffee, energy drinks, teas and smoothies, and is expanding quickly, opening more than a hundred shops a year.
customers: Young drivers who buy customised drinks on the go, and loyal app users.
money: Sales from shops Dutch Bros owns and runs.
Fees and product sales from franchised shops.
moat: A cult-like brand among young customers, fast drive-through service, and a culture its staff are known for. Its small, cheap-to-build shops pay back quickly.
risks: Growth depends on opening new shops: capital spending of $241M in 2025 ate most of the cash flow.
New shops in new states may not perform like the original ones in the West.
Coffee bean and labour costs can squeeze margins.
Diluted shares rose from 46M in 2021 to 126M in 2025, mostly from converting the founders’ ownership units.
opportunities: Revenue tripled from $498M in 2021 to $1.64B in 2025, and reached $2.0B over the last twelve months.
Net income has risen from losses to $102M over the last twelve months.
Twenty-six analysts average a target near $55, about 66% above the price.
Mobile ordering and food are adding to sales per shop.
watch: Same-shop sales growth and returns on new shops in new markets.
view: Dutch Bros is a growth story priced as one: about 42 times trailing earnings and 33 times forward. Revenue has tripled in four years and the company has turned from losses to a real profit, but almost all the cash it makes still goes into new shops, so free cash flow is small.

The question is how big the chain can get. Management talks about thousands more shops, and so far new ones have opened well outside its home region. The risk is the usual one for restaurant growth stories: as a chain expands into less familiar markets, new shops earn less, and the high multiple shrinks.

This turns on unit economics in new markets. If shops in Texas and the Southeast match those in Oregon and California, the stock can compound for years. If returns fade, it will de-rate sharply. The analysts are very optimistic; I would buy in pieces rather than all at once.
bull: Shops keep opening at strong returns and the chain reaches several thousand locations.
bear: New shops underperform outside the West and the premium multiple collapses.
